**Solution Explanation**

The FIFO queue is implemented as a *circular* buffer inside the caller‑provided array.
The function block (`FIFO`) uses the array bounds (lower‑ and upper‑index) to obtain the
queue capacity and to compute the real index that has to be written or read.
Internal state variables keep the current head and tail positions (as real array
indices) and the number of stored elements (`count`).  
Rising‑edge detection on `enqueue` and `dequeue` guarantees that only a *new*
request triggers an operation.  Reset has the highest priority and empties the
queue without overwriting the original buffer content.

The implementation follows the required interface exactly and returns the proper
status codes:

* `16#0000` – no error (idle, successful operation or reset)  
* `16#8001` – dequeue rejected because the queue is empty  
* `16#8002` – enqueue rejected because the queue is full  

All internal variables are hidden; only `elementCount` and `status` are exposed
as outputs.

---

```text
(* --------------------------------------------------
   FUNCTION BLOCK FIFO
   First‑In‑First‑Out circular queue using the caller‑supplied buffer.
   Derives capacity and element type from the buffer.
   -------------------------------------------------- *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FIFO
VAR_INPUT
    enqueue  : BOOL;      (* Rising edge → enqueue one item           *)
    dequeue  : BOOL;      (* Rising edge → dequeue one item           *)
    reset    : BOOL;      (* TRUE → empty the queue, highest priority *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    elementCount : DINT;  (* Number of valid elements (0 … capacity) *)
    status       : WORD;  (* 16#0000, 16#8001, 16#8002                *)
END_VAR
VAR_IN_OUT
    item   : VARIANT;     (* Scalar to read (enqueue) or write (dequeue) *)
    buffer : VARIANT;     (* One‑dimensional array used as storage       *)
END_VAR

VAR
    (* Internal queue state --------------------------------------------------- *)
    headIndex   : DINT;   (* Current head position (real array index)        *)
    tailIndex   : DINT;   (* Current tail position (real array index)        *)
    count       : DINT;   (* Number of stored elements (mirrors elementCount) *)

    (* Array bounds (re‑computed each cycle because buffer never changes) ----- *)
    lowerBound  : DINT;   (* LOWER_BOUND(buffer,1)                           *)
    upperBound  : DINT;   (* UPPER_BOUND(buffer,1)                           *)
    capacity    : DINT;   (* upperBound - lowerBound + 1                     *)

    (* Edge detection --------------------------------------------------------- *)
    prevEnqueue : BOOL;   (* Value of enqueue from previous cycle            *)
    prevDequeue : BOOL;   (* Value of dequeue from previous cycle            *)
    enqueueRising : BOOL; (* TRUE on a rising edge of enqueue                *)
    dequeueRising : BOOL; (* TRUE on a rising edge of dequeue                *)

    (* First‑call initialization ---------------------------------------------- *)
    initDone    : BOOL;   (* TRUE after the first execution                  *)
END_VAR

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Body of the function block                                                 *)
(* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* 1. Determine capacity from the supplied buffer ----------------------------- *)
lowerBound := LOWER_BOUND(buffer, 1);
upperBound := UPPER_BOUND(buffer, 1);
capacity   := upperBound - lowerBound + 1;

(* 2. Initialise internal variables on the very first call ------------------- *)
IF NOT initDone THEN
    headIndex := lowerBound;
    tailIndex := lowerBound;
    count     := 0;
    initDone  := TRUE;
END_IF

(* 3. Reset handling (highest priority) ------------------------------------- *)
IF reset THEN
    count     := 0;
    headIndex := lowerBound;
    tailIndex := lowerBound;
    status    := 16#0000;                     (* no error                     *)
ELSE
    (* 4. Detect rising edges on enqueue / dequeue --------------------------- *)
    enqueueRising := enqueue AND NOT prevEnqueue;
    dequeueRising := dequeue AND NOT prevDequeue;

    (* Store current input states for next cycle ----------------------------- *)
    prevEnqueue := enqueue;
    prevDequeue := dequeue;

    (* Default status = no error -------------------------------------------- *)
    status := 16#0000;

    (* 5. Enqueue request ----------------------------------------------------- *)
    IF enqueueRising THEN
        IF count < capacity THEN
            (* Append the current item to the tail -------------------------- *)
            buffer[tailIndex] := item;

            (* Advance tail (circular) -------------------------------------- *)
            tailIndex := tailIndex + 1;
            IF tailIndex > upperBound THEN
                tailIndex := lowerBound;
            END_IF

            count := count + 1;
        ELSE
            (* Queue full – reject the request -------------------------------- *)
            status := 16#8002;
        END_IF
    END_IF

    (* 6. Dequeue request ----------------------------------------------------- *)
    IF dequeueRising THEN
        IF count > 0 THEN
            (* Copy the front element to item -------------------------------- *)
            item := buffer[headIndex];

            (* Advance head (circular) --------------------------------------- *)
            headIndex := headIndex + 1;
            IF headIndex > upperBound THEN
                headIndex := lowerBound;
            END_IF

            count := count - 1;
        ELSE
            (* Queue empty – reject the request ------------------------------- *)
            status := 16#8001;
        END_IF
    END_IF
END_IF

(* 7. Publish the current number of stored elements -------------------------- *)
elementCount := count;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

**Explanation of key design choices**

* **Circular wrap‑around** – `headIndex` and `tailIndex` are increased after each
  dequeue/enqueue and wrapped to `lowerBound` when they exceed `upperBound`.
* **Rising‑edge detection** – `prevEnqueue` / `prevDequeue` store the input
  values from the previous PLC cycle; a new request is recognised only when the
  input changes from `FALSE` to `TRUE`.
* **Capacity derivation** – `LOWER_BOUND` and `UPPER_BOUND` are evaluated each
  cycle, guaranteeing that the function block works with any one‑dimensional
  array (static or dynamic) without prior knowledge of its size.
* **Reset priority** – When `reset` is `TRUE` the queue is cleared (`count := 0`)
  and the indices are reset to the array’s lower bound; the buffer content is
  left untouched as required.
* **Status reporting** – The output `status` is set to `16#8001` (empty) or
  `16#8002` (full) only when a request is rejected; otherwise it remains
  `16#0000` (including idle and successful operations).

This implementation satisfies all requirements of the specification.
